changelog:
Introduce multi-OS build matrix and a separate release job that aggregates artifacts, computes SHA-256 checksums, and generates detailed release_notes.md. Update CI to rename and upload per-platform artifacts and download them in the release step; extract version from tag and publish GitHub releases with all assets. Change update.json to point to the Setup installer.

Packaging/desktop: improve Packager platform detection and support Linux outputs; add robust electron-builder artifact discovery. electron/main.js: add downloadFile and startAutoUpdate (progress UI, automatic installer launch), expand update dialog options and better error/status handling. electron/package.json: add Linux targets and explicit artifact naming for Setup/Portable installers.

App fixes: routes/info.py trims duplicate filename markers and improves platform labeling by inferring from extractor or the request URL. static/js/main.js replaces a simple confirm() with the app showConfirm modal for clearing download history.

Overall this changeset enables multi-platform releases, automated release notes/checksums, and a smoother in-app update flow.

On macOS/Linux, replace pkill -f with pkill -x for matching exact process names (server and EveryThingDownloader) to avoid the build script matching its own command-line and terminating itself (exit code 143). Adds a clarifying comment and keeps behavior of terminating running app/server instances to release file locks.

Add a `maintainer` entry to the `linux` section of electron/package.json: `EveryThingDownloader <contact@everythingdownloader.com>`. This adds contact information for the Linux build artifacts (AppImage, tar.gz) and may be required by some packaging tools or distribution metadata consumers.

Include the project's GitHub URL in electron/package.json via the "homepage" field (https://github.com/m3iK18dp/EveryThingDownloader-Tool). This adds canonical project metadata used by package tooling and consumer-facing pages.

Make releases and packaged artifacts architecture-aware. Update CI and git_helper to publish darwin_arm64/darwin_x64 and linux_x64 release URLs. Change packager and electron/package.json to append -${arch} to dmg/pkg/deb/rpm (and add zip and tar.gz), and update electron main to generate/resolve filenames using process.arch and to prefer platform_arch keys with fallbacks. This enables per-architecture downloads for multi-arch builds.

Add cleanup of previous build assets in builder_cli.py (remove dist and dist_electron, fall back to deleting individual files while skipping _protected) to avoid leftover artifacts interfering with new builds. Update packager.py to use generic mac/linux artifactName patterns that include ${ext} instead of many per-format entries. Update electron/package.json to set top-level and linux artifactName fields and remove redundant per-format artifact entries for simpler, consistent output naming.

Add steps to the build-and-release workflow to delete any existing release assets for the current tag in both the private and public repositories before creating/uploading new assets. The steps use the gh CLI (gh release view + gh release delete-asset) and set GH_TOKEN/RELEASE_TOKEN accordingly. Also corrects a comment typo. This prevents duplicate-asset errors when the workflow is re-run.

Add short delays and logging when launching downloaded installers. On Linux, wrap AppImage execution in a bash 'sleep 2 && exec "dest"' to allow a graceful exit and avoid port conflicts; chmod remains applied. On Windows, run a cmd.exe wrapper that pings localhost to delay, attempts to kill lingering processes (server.exe and EveryThingDownloader.exe), then starts the installer. Also add log.info messages and ensure the child is detached/unref'd; shell=true is enabled for the Windows spawn.

Rework GitHub Actions release steps: update update.json, commit and force-create the release tag in the public repo before uploading built assets, then clean and upload assets using softprops/action-gh-release (now passing tag_name). Adds git tagging/force-push to ensure the public repo tag matches the current release. In electron/main.js, compute the running EXE name (from process.execPath) and use it in the Windows delayed installer launcher so taskkill targets the actual app process instead of a hardcoded filename.
